z_authors is deprecated; use OpenAlex authorships instead
oa_date is currently the publication date for every location — do not use it for embargo checks
closed / no-location records are valid outcomes, not errors

auth.api_key: optional — keyless access allowed for casual use; free email-activated key (POST /api-keys) gives 10x daily budget and is required for cursor paging past page 1
auth.note: Key states: no key, or a key with a verified email; unactivated key -> 403 key_not_activated; key env-var pattern OPENALEX_API_KEY matches doc guidance

rate_limit.model: USD daily budget (credits), not a fixed calls-per-window quota
rate_limit.new_account_pace: first $1 at up to $0.10 every 5 minutes (~50 min of steady use)
rate_limit.retry_after: 429 bodies give wait seconds; doc: 'Wait the Retry-After seconds (usually 1) and retry'

pagination.mechanism: basic: page & per_page (per_page 1-100; page*per_page <= 10000) + cursor: cursor=* then follow meta.next_cursor; cursor paging past page 1 requires a free API key (keyless follow -> 401)
pagination.note: Do not cursor-page the whole dataset; use the monthly snapshot instead. per_page=200 still accepted as deprecated legacy behavior.

discovery_filters_confirmed: open_access.is_oa (filter) / open_access (select; nested object with is_oa, oa_status, oa_url, any_repository_has_fulltext)
gotchas: open_access is nested: filter open_access.is_oa:true, select the open_access object (selecting open_access.is_oa directly -> 400)
OR (|) max 100 values per single filter; OR only within one filter, not between filters
+ decodes to space = AND inside filter values; quote values containing spaces
comma inside a value -> wrap value in double quotes
complex boolean searches (>5 operators) and wide OR topic filters and semantic search have lower 1/s limits
basic paging capped at 10,000 results; beyond that cursor paging (needs key)

spec_claims_verification.claim: Default (no API key) 'polite pool' rate limit
spec_claims_verification.doc_says: No 'polite pool' term exists in current docs; keyless = $0.10/day budget + 10 req/s per IP

spec_claims_verification.claim: Activated API key ~100k calls per 5 minutes
spec_claims_verification.doc_says: Free key = $1/day budget (10x keyless); $0.10 per 1000 list+filter calls => ~10,000 list calls/day, ~1,000 search calls/day; per-second caps 30/s; the $0.10/5-min pace applies only to the FIRST dollar of a NEW account. No 100k-calls/5min figure in the docs.
pacing.md: 'cursor=* works, but following next_cursor returns a 401' without a key; free key required past page 1; basic paging limit 10,000
filtering.md lists publication_year, from/to_publication_date, type, open_access.is_oa for works

spec_claims_verification.claim: Require an activated account key for the overnight profile when pagination needs it
spec_claims_verification.doc_says: Keyless cursor paging stops at the first page; deep pagination needs the free key

auth.polite_pool: mailto query param: 'The email address to identify yourself and access the polite pool' (OpenAPI spec); example in REST API doc: /works?rows=0&mailto=yourmail@company.org
auth.note: 'No sign-up is required to use the REST API'

rate_limit.published: No single hard quota number published in the doc text
rate_limit.observed_polite_pool: live 2026-11-18 headers on a mailto request: x-rate-limit-limit: 3, x-rate-limit-interval: 1s, x-concurrency-limit: 3, x-api-pool: polite-array (~3 req/s in polite pool)
rate_limit.note: API handles 'over two billion calls per month'; a live un-pooled GET / returned 429. Honor 429 + backoff; treat polite pool as ~3 req/s

pagination.mechanism: rows (page size, up to 1000/list request) + offset (skip <= 10,000) + cursor: cursor=* -> next-cursor in response -> cursor=<next>; 'Cursors expire after 5 minutes'; stop when items < rows; docs recommend cursors over offset

key_endpoints: GET https://api.crossref.org/works (list; query.bibliographic, query.title, query, filter, facet, sort, select, cursor, rows, offset, mailto)
crossref.response_format: JSON (application/vnd.crossref-api-message+json); select param trims fields; HEAD returns headers-only existence check; content negotiation for singletons (XML/BibTeX/Citation styles)
gotchas: URL-encode DOIs in paths (10.1128%2Fmbio...)
Facet counts are approximate; records with multiple relationships are counted multiple times
No /events endpoint in the current spec (live GET /events -> 404 route-not-found)
query.bibliographic only searches reference fields (title, authors, volume, journal name, etc.)
Cursors expire after 5 minutes if unused
Some abstracts may be subject to publisher/author copyright even though most metadata is not

auth.note: No auth for the metadata API. Noncommercial projects: include the acknowledgement 'Thank you to arXiv for use of its open access interoperability'; commercial projects must review brand guidelines / consider arXivLabs affiliation

rate_limit.published: TOU: 'When using the legacy APIs (including OAI-PMH, RSS, and the arXiv API), make no more than one request every three seconds, and limit requests to a single connection at a time. These limits may change in the future.'
rate_limit.scope: applies to all machines under your control as a whole; TOU forbids splitting across machines to beat the limit

pagination.mechanism: start (0-based offset) + max_results (page size); no cursor
pagination.note: Docs examples use max_results=10; no cap on max_results is stated in the fetched pages — verify before bulk pulls

key_endpoints: GET http://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=id1,id2 (id lookup; no version suffix = latest version)
arxiv.response_format: Atom 1.0 XML feed with OpenSearch extension elements (opensearch:totalResults, startIndex, itemsPerPage); errors are Atom feeds with a single entry (summary + link to explanation)

url_patterns.abs: https://arxiv.org/abs/{id}v{n} (live-verified: requesting id without suffix returns latest-version link, e.g. .../abs/cond-mat/0207270v3)

arxiv.version_identity: First posting = v1; each resubmission increments; 'if you want to retrieve the latest version ... enter the arxiv id in the id_list'; 'to retrieve information about a specific version ... appending vn to the id'. Store the vN that appears in <id>/links, not the bare id.
gotchas: abs/pdf links always carry a vN suffix even when the request id had none
Pacing: max 1 request per 3 s on a single connection across all your machines; no documented 429/Retry-After
Malformed ids return an Atom error feed (summary message + link), not JSON
max_results cap for bulk pulls is not documented in the fetched pages
